source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Remain flat for several hours after the procedure because prolonged bed rest has been shown to prevent post-dural-puncture headache after lumbar puncture.","B":"Drink extra fluids specifically to prevent headache because aggressive hydration has been shown to stop cerebrospinal-fluid leakage after lumbar puncture.","C":"Avoid upright activity until the next day because sitting or walking after lumbar puncture is known to increase persistent cerebrospinal-fluid leakage.","D":"Prolonged bed rest is not shown to prevent post-puncture headache; follow postprocedure instructions and mobilize as clinically appropriate when allowed."}}
source_row.rationale: Current evidence does not support routine prolonged bed rest after lumbar puncture solely to prevent post-dural-puncture headache; Cochrane found that bed rest does not prevent the headache and may increase it, and extra fluids have not shown preventive benefit. Option D is correct. Option A incorrectly claims prolonged flat positioning is preventive. Option B overstates hydration as a preventive intervention. Option C incorrectly treats upright activity as a proven cause of persistent CSF leakage. Specific postprocedure instructions should still be followed for other clinical reasons.
source_row.source_detail: Cochrane Review CD009199 — Body position and intake of fluids for preventing headache after a lumbar puncture: routine bed rest after lumbar puncture does not prevent post-dural-puncture headache and may increase its occurrence; extra fluid intake has not shown preventive benefit. Routine prolonged flat positioning solely for prevention is not supported. Cochrane systematic review published 2016-03-07 remains the active evidence review at the cited source; currentness and absence of a superseding Cochrane conclusion rechecked 2026-08-15. Blueprint corrected to Reduction of Risk Potential because the item tests prevention of a complication after a diagnostic procedure, explicitly represented in the 2026 NCSBN test plan. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Reduction of Risk Potential: diagnostic probability tools, laboratory/tumor-marker interpretation, ECG/lab monitoring and potential complications. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
